fixes.explanation: Making peace with Esau would be a lovely ending, but this passage doesn't give it. Esau is Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24–26), and these verses never mention him. That's like handing out the cookie box before anybody has even turned on the oven. Jacob's reason for the name is, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30).

That's the reason the text gives, baker. “…the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The verse starts with “Therefore to this day…” so the practice was still going when this was written. One night at the river, and the Israelites were still keeping it all those years later. I can't keep a New Year's resolution past February, and this habit outlasted all of mine.

problems.problem: It uses a dash. No em dashes or en dashes.
The comparison doesn't click: putting sprinkles on a cookie before baking is normal, so it doesn't convey bringing in an event the passage hasn't given.
The passage gives the reason for the practice, but it doesn't say that the whole people remember Jacob's injury at the table.
